mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 0.25% over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 0.25% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 6% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for S&P 500 constituents and leads to negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the unemployment rate and initial jobless claims (PAYEMS negative, RSAFS negative) signals a deteriorating labor market, which increases recession risk and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in both real personal income (implied by GDPC1 growth) and retail sales (HOUST) above their respective 12-month averages signals robust consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both above 12-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +2%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held below 1% for more than six consecutive months in a low-inflation environment signals accommodative monetary policy, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% for more than six consecutive months and CPIAUCSL < 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1% coincident with a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a synchronized supply and labor shock, which increases recession probability and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -4%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
